CodeIgniter

Complete Spark Command Reference & Concept Guide v4.x PHP 7.4+ PHP 8.x Ready

CodeIgniter is a powerful PHP framework with a tiny footprint, built for developers who need a simple and elegant toolkit to create full-featured web applications. This guide covers all Spark CLI commands, core concepts, and practical code examples for CodeIgniter 4.

Installation

# Install via Composer

composer create-project codeigniter4/appstarter myapp

# Or download the zip from GitHub

# https://github.com/codeigniter4/CodeIgniter4/releases

# Start the development server

php spark serve

# Specify host and port

php spark serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

# With live reload (requires PHP 8.1+)

php spark serve --reload

Directory Structure

myapp/
  app/
    Config/         # Configuration files
    Controllers/    # Controllers
    Database/
      Migrations/   # Database migrations
      Seeds/        # Database seeds
    Entities/       # Entity classes (optional)
    Filters/        # Filter / middleware classes
    Helpers/        # Custom helper files
    Language/       # Language files
    Libraries/      # Custom libraries
    Models/         # Models
    Views/          # View files
  public/           # Document root
    index.php       # Front controller
    .htaccess       # Apache rewrite rules
  system/           # CI4 framework files
  writable/         # Writable directory (logs, cache)
  .env              # Environment configuration
  spark             # CLI entry point

Spark CLI Commands Reference

All commands run via php spark <command> from the application root.

Code Generation

CommandDescription
spark make:controller <name>Generate a new controller file
spark make:model <name>Generate a new model file
spark make:entity <name>Generate a new entity class
spark make:migration <name>Generate a new migration file
spark make:seeder <name>Generate a new database seeder
spark make:filter <name>Generate a new filter class
spark make:command <name>Generate a new spark command
spark make:config <name>Generate a new config file
spark make:validation <name>Generate a new validation file
spark make:cell <name>Generate a new view cell

Database / Migrations

CommandDescription
spark migrateRun all pending migrations
spark migrate --allRun pending migrations from all namespaces
spark migrate:rollbackRoll back the last batch of migrations
spark migrate:refreshRoll back and re-run all migrations
spark migrate:statusShow migration status for all namespaces
spark db:seed <name>Run a database seeder

Cache

CommandDescription
spark cache:clearClear all system caches
spark cache:infoShow cache file information

Routes

CommandDescription
spark routesDisplay all registered routes
spark routes --hostShow routes filtered by hostname

Utilities

CommandDescription

spark serve --reloadStart dev server with live reload (PHP 8.1+)

spark listList all available spark commands
spark help <cmd>Get help for a specific command

spark db:table <name>Show table information

MVC Architecture

Model

Business logic & data access. Interacts with the database.

app/Models/

Request handling, flow control, data passing to views.

app/Controllers/
View

Presentation layer. HTML templates with PHP.

app/Views/

Routing

Define routes in app/Config/Routes.php. CodeIgniter 4 uses a flexible routing system with auto-routing and defined routes.

Basic Routing
// app/Config/Routes.php

use CodeIgniter\Router\RouteCollection;

// Auto-routing (disabled by default in v4.5+)

$routes->setAutoRoute(true);

// Simple route

$routes->get('/', 'Home::index');

// Route with parameters

$routes->get('blog/(:segment)', 'Blog::view/$1');

// Named routes

$routes->get('articles/(:num)', 'Articles::show/$1')
    ->setName('article_view');

// Route groups

$routes->group('admin', ['filter' => 'login'], function ($routes) {
    $routes->get('dashboard', 'Admin::dashboard');
    $routes->resource('users');
});

// HTTP method routes

$routes->get('products', 'Product::index');
$routes->post('products', 'Product::create');
$routes->put('products/(:num)', 'Product::update/$1');
$routes->delete('products/(:num)', 'Product::delete/$1');

// Closures

$routes->get('info', function () {
    return 'Hello World';
});

// Environment-specific routes

$routes->environment('development', function ($routes) {
    $routes->get('debug', 'Debug::index');
});

// View routes (direct to view without controller)

$routes->view('about', 'about_page');

Resource Route Mapping

HTTP MethodURLController ActionRoute Name
GET/usersUser::index()users
GET/users/newUser::new()users.new
GET/users/{id}User::show($id)users.show
GET/users/{id}/editUser::edit($id)users.edit
POST/usersUser::create()users.create
PUT/PATCH/users/{id}User::update($id)users.update
DELETE/users/{id}User::delete($id)users.delete
Placeholder Patterns: (:any) — matches any character, (:segment) — single segment, (:num) — numeric only, (:alpha) — alphabetic only, (:alphanum) — alphanumeric only.

Controllers

User Controller — CRUD Example
// app/Controllers/User.php

namespace App\Controllers;

use App\Models\UserModel;
use CodeIgniter\HTTP\RedirectResponse;

class User extends BaseController
{
    protected $helpers = ['form', 'url'];

    public function index(): string
    {
        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $data['users'] = $userModel->paginate(10);
        $data['pager'] = $userModel->pager;
        return view('user/index', $data);
    }

    public function show($id = null): string
    {
        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $data['user'] = $userModel->find($id);
        if (!$data['user']) {
            throw new \CodeIgniter\Exceptions\PageNotFoundException('User not found');
        }
        return view('user/show', $data);
    }

    public function new(): string
    {
        return view('user/new');
    }

    public function create(): RedirectResponse
    {
        $rules = [
            'name'  => 'required|min_length[3]|max_length[255]',
            'email' => 'required|valid_email|is_unique[users.email]',
        ];

        if (!$this->validate($rules)) {
            return redirect()->back()->withInput()
                ->with('errors', $this->validator->getErrors());
        }

        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $userModel->save([
            'name'  => $this->request->getPost('name'),
            'email' => $this->request->getPost('email'),
        ]);

        return redirect()->to('users')->with('message', 'User created');
    }

    public function edit($id = null): string
    {
        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $data['user'] = $userModel->find($id);
        return view('user/edit', $data);
    }

    public function update($id = null): RedirectResponse
    {
        $rules = [
            'name'  => 'required|min_length[3]|max_length[255]',
            'email' => "required|valid_email|is_unique[users.email,id,{$id}]",
        ];

        if (!$this->validate($rules)) {
            return redirect()->back()->withInput()
                ->with('errors', $this->validator->getErrors());
        }

        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $userModel->update($id, [
            'name'  => $this->request->getPost('name'),
            'email' => $this->request->getPost('email'),
        ]);

        return redirect()->to('users')->with('message', 'User updated');
    }

    public function delete($id = null): RedirectResponse
    {
        $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
        $userModel->delete($id);
        return redirect()->to('users')->with('message', 'User deleted');
    }
}

Base Controller Features

BaseController.php
namespace App\Controllers;

use CodeIgniter\HTTP\RequestInterface;
use CodeIgniter\HTTP\ResponseInterface;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

abstract class BaseController extends \CodeIgniter\Controller
{
    protected RequestInterface $request;
    protected ResponseInterface $response;
    protected LoggerInterface $logger;
    protected $helpers = [];

    public function initController(
        RequestInterface $request,
        ResponseInterface $response,
        LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {
        $this->request  = $request;
        $this->response = $response;
        $this->logger   = $logger;
    }
}

namespace App\Models;

class UserModel extends Model
{
    protected $table            = 'users';
    protected $primaryKey       = 'id';
    protected $useAutoIncrement = true;
    protected $returnType       = 'array';
    protected $useSoftDeletes   = true;
    protected $protectFields    = true;
    protected $allowedFields    = ['name', 'email', 'password'];

    // Dates

    protected $useTimestamps = true;
    protected $dateFormat    = 'datetime';
    protected $createdField  = 'created_at';
    protected $updatedField  = 'updated_at';
    protected $deletedField  = 'deleted_at';

    // Validation

    protected $validationRules = [
        'name'  => 'required|min_length[3]|max_length[255]',
        'email' => 'required|valid_email|is_unique[users.email]',
    ];
    protected $validationMessages = [
        'email' => [
            'is_unique' => 'This email is already registered.',
        ],
    ];
    protected $skipValidation = false;
    protected $cleanValidationRules = true;
}

Migrations

Migration Example
namespace App\Database\Migrations;

use CodeIgniter\Database\Migration;

class CreateUsersTable extends Migration
{
    public function up()
    {
        $this->forge->addField([
            'id' => [
                'type'           => 'INT',
                'constraint'     => 11,
                'unsigned'       => true,
                'auto_increment' => true,
            ],
            'name' => [
                'type'       => 'VARCHAR',
                'constraint' => '255',
            ],
            'email' => [
                'type'       => 'VARCHAR',
                'constraint' => '255',
                'unique'     => true,
            ],
            'created_at' => [
                'type' => 'DATETIME',
                'null' => true,
            ],
            'updated_at' => [
                'type' => 'DATETIME',
                'null' => true,
            ],
            'deleted_at' => [
                'type' => 'DATETIME',
                'null' => true,
            ],
        ]);
        $this->forge->addKey('id', true);
        $this->forge->createTable('users');
    }

    public function down()
    {
        $this->forge->dropTable('users');
    }
}

Query Builder

CodeIgniter's Query Builder provides a simple, fluent interface for database operations.

Read Queries
$db = db_connect();

// Basic select

$query = $db->table('users')->get();
$users = $query->getResult();

// Select specific columns

$users = $db->table('users')
    ->select('id, name, email')
    ->where('active', 1)
    ->orderBy('created_at', 'DESC')
    ->limit(10)
    ->get()
    ->getResultArray();

// Single row

$user = $db->table('users')->where('id', 1)->get()->getRow();

// Count

$count = $db->table('users')->where('active', 1)->countAllResults();

// LIKE

$users = $db->table('users')
    ->like('name', 'john')
    ->orLike('email', 'john')
    ->get()
    ->getResult();

// Join

$users = $db->table('users')
    ->select('users.*, profiles.bio')
    ->join('profiles', 'profiles.user_id = users.id', 'left')
    ->get()
    ->getResult();
Write Queries
$db = db_connect();

// Insert

$db->table('users')->insert([
    'name'  => 'John Doe',
    'email' => 'john@example.com',
]);
// $db->insertID()

// Insert batch

$db->table('users')->insertBatch([
    ['name' => 'Jane', 'email' => 'jane@example.com'],
    ['name' => 'Bob', 'email' => 'bob@example.com'],
]);

// Update

$db->table('users')
    ->where('id', 1)
    ->update(['name' => 'Jane Doe']);

// Delete

$db->table('users')->where('id', 1)->delete();

// Transactions

$db->transStart();
$db->table('accounts')->where('id', 1)
    ->set('balance', 'balance - 100', false)
    ->update();
$db->table('accounts')->where('id', 2)
    ->set('balance', 'balance + 100', false)
    ->update();
$db->transComplete();

Validation

CodeIgniter 4 provides a powerful validation library with a huge set of built-in rules.

Controller Validation
// In controller

$rules = [
    'name'     => 'required|min_length[3]|max_length[255]',
    'email'    => 'required|valid_email|is_unique[users.email]',
    'password' => 'required|min_length[8]',
    'age'      => 'permit_empty|numeric|greater_than[0]|less_than[150]',
    'website'  => 'permit_empty|valid_url',
    'gender'   => 'in_list[male,female,other]',
];

if ($this->validate($rules)) {
    // Valid

} else {
    // Get errors

    $errors = $this->validator->getErrors();
}
Validation with Custom Errors
$rules = [
    'password' => 'required|min_length[8]|strong_password',
];

$errors = [
    'password' => [
        'min_length'     => 'Password must be at least 8 characters.',
        'strong_password' => 'Password must contain uppercase, lowercase, digit and symbol.',
    ],
];

if (!$this->validate($rules, $errors)) {
    dd($this->validator->getErrors());
}

Common Validation Rules

RuleDescription
requiredField must not be empty
valid_emailMust be a valid email format
valid_urlMust be a valid URL
min_length[N]Minimum length N characters
max_length[N]Maximum length N characters
exact_length[N]Exact length N characters
numericMust be numeric
integerMust be an integer
greater_than[N]Greater than N
less_than[N]Less than N
alphaOnly alphabetic characters
alpha_numericAlphanumeric only
matches[field]Must match another field
differs[field]Must differ from another field
is_unique[table.field]Unique in database column
in_list[a,b,c]Must be one of the listed values
regex_match[/pattern/]Must match regex pattern
uploaded[name]File was uploaded
max_size[name,N]File max size in KB
ext_in[name,exts]File must have allowed extension

Views & Layouts

CodeIgniter uses simple PHP-based templates. Views are stored in app/Views/.

Basic View
// In controller:

$data['title'] = 'User Profile';
$data['user']  = $userModel->find(1);
return view('user/profile', $data);

// app/Views/user/profile.php

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title><?= esc($title) ?></title>
</head>
<body>
    <h1><?= esc($user['name']) ?></h1>

</body>

$this->endSection();

$this->section('content');
?>

<?php

?>

<?php $this->endSection();
View Cells (Reusable Components)
// app/Cells/RecentPostsCell.php

namespace App\Cells;

use CodeIgniter\View\Cells\Cell;

class RecentPostsCell extends Cell
{
    protected string $view = 'components/recent_posts';

    public function mount(int $limit = 5): void
    {
        $posts = model('PostModel')
            ->orderBy('created_at', 'DESC')
            ->findAll($limit);
        $this->data(compact('posts'));
    }
}

// In view:

Sessions & Authentication

Sessions

// In controller

$session = session();

// Set

$session->set('user_id', 1);
$session->set(['name' => 'John', 'role' => 'admin']);

// Get

$userId = $session->get('user_id');

Authentication Example

Login / Auth Helper
namespace App\Controllers;

use App\Models\UserModel;

class Auth extends BaseController
{
    protected $helpers = ['form'];

    public function login()
    {
        $rules = [
            'email'    => 'required|valid_email',
            'password' => 'required',
        ];

        if ($this->request->getMethod() === 'POST' && $this->validate($rules)) {
            $userModel = model(UserModel::class);
            $user = $userModel->where('email', $this->request->getPost('email'))
                ->first();

            if ($user && password_verify(
                $this->request->getPost('password'),
                $user['password_hash']
            )) {
                session()->set([
                    'user_id' => $user['id'],
                    'isLoggedIn' => true,
                ]);
                return redirect()->to('dashboard');
            }

            session()->setFlashdata('error', 'Invalid credentials');
        }

        return view('auth/login');
    }

    public function logout()
    {
        session()->destroy();
        return redirect()->to('login');
    }
}

// Auth filter (app/Filters/AuthFilter.php)

namespace App\Filters;

use CodeIgniter\HTTP\RequestInterface;
use CodeIgniter\HTTP\ResponseInterface;
use CodeIgniter\Filters\FilterInterface;

class AuthFilter implements FilterInterface
{
    public function before(RequestInterface $request)
    {
        if (!session()->get('isLoggedIn')) {
            return redirect()->to('login');
        }
    }

    public function after(RequestInterface $request, ResponseInterface $response) {}
}

// Register: app/Config/Filters.php

$filters->aliases(['auth' => \App\Filters\AuthFilter::class]);

// Apply to routes

$routes->group('admin', ['filter' => 'auth'], function ($routes) {
    $routes->get('dashboard', 'Admin::dashboard');
});

RESTful API

CodeIgniter makes it easy to build REST APIs with its built-in request handling and response formatting.

API Controller
namespace App\Controllers\Api;

use CodeIgniter\HTTP\ResponseInterface;
use App\Models\UserModel;

class Users extends \CodeIgniter\RESTful\ResourceController
{
    protected $modelName = UserModel::class;
    protected $format    = 'json';

    public function index()
    {
        $users = $this->model->findAll();
        return $this->respond(['data' => $users]);
    }

    public function show($id = null)
    {
        $user = $this->model->find($id);
        if (!$user) {
            return $this->failNotFound('User not found');
        }
        return $this->respond(['data' => $user]);
    }

    public function create()
    {
        $rules = [
            'name'  => 'required|min_length[3]',
            'email' => 'required|valid_email|is_unique[users.email]',
        ];

        if (!$this->validate($rules)) {
            return $this->fail($this->validator->getErrors());
        }

        $id = $this->model->insert(
            $this->request->getJSON()
        );

        return $this->respondCreated(['id' => $id]);
    }

    public function update($id = null)
    {
        $data = $this->request->getJSON();
        $this->model->update($id, $data);
        return $this->respondUpdated(['data' => $id]);
    }

    public function delete($id = null)
    {
        $this->model->delete($id);
        return $this->respondDeleted(['id' => $id]);
    }
}

// Routes

$routes->resource('api/users', [
    'controller' => 'Api\Users',
    'only'       => ['index', 'show', 'create', 'update', 'delete'],
]);
Response Helpers
$this->respond($data, 200);
$this->respondCreated($data);       // 201
$this->respondDeleted($data);       // 200
$this->respondUpdated($data);       // 200
$this->failUnauthorized('Unauthorized');  // 401
$this->failForbidden('Forbidden');       // 403
$this->failNotFound('Not found');         // 404
$this->failValidationError($errors);        // 422
$this->failServerError('Server error');    // 500

CORS for API
// app/Config/Filters.php

public $globals = [
    'before' => [
        'cors'
    ],
];

// app/Filters/CorsFilter.php

class CorsFilter implements FilterInterface
{
    public function before(RequestInterface $request)
    {
        if ($request->getMethod() === 'OPTIONS') {
            return response()->setStatusCode(204)
                ->setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*')
                ->setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS')
                ->setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'Content-Type, Authorization');
        }
    }

    public function after(RequestInterface $request, ResponseInterface $response) {}
}

Services & Dependency Injection

CodeIgniter uses a Services pattern for dependency injection.

Using Services
use Config\Services;

$email = Services::email();
$throttler = Services::throttler();
$timer = Services::timer();
$renderer = Services::renderer();
$cache = Services::cache();
$curlrequest = Services::curlrequest();
$session = Services::session();
$encrypter = Services::encrypter();
$security = Services::security();
Sending Email
$email = \Config\Services::email();
$email->setFrom('from@example.com', 'Admin');
$email->setTo('to@example.com');
$email->setSubject('Welcome');
$email->setMessage('Thank you for registering.');

if ($email->send()) {
    // Success

} else {
    $error = $email->printDebugger(['headers']);
}
Caching
$cache = \Config\Services::cache();

// Store

$cache->save('key', $data, 3600);  // 1 hour

// Retrieve

$data = $cache->get('key');

// Delete

$cache->delete('key');

// Clear all

$cache->clean();

Testing

CodeIgniter 4 has built-in testing support using PHPUnit.

Controller Test
namespace Tests\Controller;

use CodeIgniter\Test\ControllerTestTrait;
use CodeIgniter\Test\CIUnitTestCase;
use Config\Services;

class UserControllerTest extends CIUnitTestCase
{
    use ControllerTestTrait;

    public function testIndex(): void
    {
        $result = $this->withUri('http://localhost/users')
            ->controller(\App\Controllers\User::class)
            ->run('index');

        $this->assertStringContainsString('Users', $result);
    }

    public function testCreateValidatesInput(): void
    {
        $result = $this->withBody([
            'name'  => '',
            'email' => 'invalid',
        ])->controller(\App\Controllers\User::class)
            ->run('create');

        $this->assertInstanceOf(\CodeIgniter\HTTP\RedirectResponse::class, $result);
    }

Key Guidelines
  • Always use esc() when outputting user data
  • Use models for all database interactions
  • Keep controllers thin; use models/libraries
  • Use migrations for schema version control
  • Enable CSRF protection for web routes
  • Use .env for environment config
  • Use filters for cross-cutting concerns
  • Set CI_ENVIRONMENT = production in production
  • Never commit .env or writable/ files
  • Use entity classes for data logic
